question: Which mechanism leads to the folding of Mimosa pudica leaves when they are touched?

options.text: Change in pH of leaf cells
Change in the water content of leaf cells
Change in light intensity at leaf surface
Change in temperature of the leaves

solution:
The correct answer is __**Change in the water content of leaf cells**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Mimosa pudica**, commonly known as the "touch-me-not" plant, exhibits a phenomenon known as thigmonasty, where the leaves fold upon touch or mechanical stimulus.
 
• This movement results from a rapid change in the turgor pressure of cells in specialised structures called the pulvini at the bases of the leaflets and petioles.
 
• When stimulated, ions like potassium (K⁺) are pumped out of the cells in the pulvini, causing water to exit the cells via osmosis. This leads to a loss of turgidity in the cells, resulting in the folding of the leaves.
 
• This reaction is a defensive mechanism believed to protect the plant from herbivores or environmental stressors, as the sudden movement might deter predators.
